details: CONFIRMED by a repro: recording with RELAY_HOME=testA and reading with RELAY_HOME=testB gives "not sent by relay".
The per-test switch is documented in tests/conftest.py:1 and done in tests/tmp_default.py temporary_environment
(RELAY_HOME per test), which does not list RELAY_SIGNAL_LOG. Inside a gate the inherited RELAY_SIGNAL_LOG hides it,
but the worker's own loop (bin/check, plain pytest) is where flaky SIGTERMs are first met, and the line there states a
false fact. The cleanest fix is one log per test run, fixed before the per-test switch; where it lives is Q in F2.
Size: 15 minutes.
evidence: gate command ended by SIGTERM, not sent by relay (no record of it in .../sig/testB/.relay/signals.log)
tests/tmp_default.py:43: "RELAY_HOME": os.path.join(base, ".relay"),   (per test; RELAY_SIGNAL_LOG not handled)
failing_case: A worker loops on bin/check --tests tests/test_gate.py (no outer gate, so RELAY_SIGNAL_LOG is unset). tests/tmp_default.py
gives every test its own RELAY_HOME, so signal_log() is <test-temp>/.relay/signals.log, different per test. Test A's
gate sweeps a leftover and SIGTERMs pid 4242, recording it in A's log; test B's gate, whose command is 4242, reads B's
log. Now: "gate command ended by SIGTERM, not sent by relay (no record of it in .../testB/.relay/signals.log)".
Should: name relay's sweep as the sender (or at least not claim it was not relay).
fix_hint: Pin RELAY_SIGNAL_LOG once per run before the per-test switch (tests/conftest.py pytest_sessionstart and
tests/run_unittest.py / parallel_unittest.py: if unset, set it to the run's log), so every test of a run and its
workers share one file. Where that file is: see F2.
pass_cases: 1. Two processes with different RELAY_HOME and no RELAY_SIGNAL_LOG inside one test run: one records a SIGTERM to pid N, the other's signal_line(15, N, t0) says "sent by relay: ... leftover sweep" (both resolve the same log for the run).
2. Under a gate (RELAY_SIGNAL_LOG set by relay_gate.run): unchanged, tests and the gate share that log.
3. A SIGTERM with no record anywhere: still "not sent by relay" (test_a_gate_command_ended_by_a_signal_leaves_a_line_in_the_gate_log).
4. test_a_stop_relay_sends_to_the_command_is_named_in_the_gate_log keeps passing.
reason: Carried over from the earlier check; files unchanged since.
findings.summary: outside a gate each test has its own RELAY_HOME, so the signal log is split per test and a stop relay sent from another test is reported as 'not sent by relay'

details: CONFIRMED (measured 48 lines for one test file of 37 tests). Why this is a question: the 29 Oct SIGTERM hit a nested gate
inside a test, and the sender may have been another lane's gate (its sweep). Only a machine-wide log (the live
~/.relay one) lets a test's nested gate see a stop another lane sent; a run-wide temporary log keeps tests out of
~/.relay but cannot attribute a cross-lane stop, and its records vanish with the run. The change took the first
without saying so and without a bound on the file.
Intro for the owner: relay now keeps one shared file of every stop signal it sends, and a gate log line says
"sent by relay: <that line>" or "not sent by relay". Tests run gates inside gates; for the record to reach the nested
gate, tests must write the same file. Live example: one test file wrote 48 lines.
Options: (a) tests write the machine-wide file (cross-lane stops are named; the file needs a size bound; the test
harness rule gets one named exception); (b) each test run has its own temporary file (tests never touch ~/.relay;
a stop from another lane's gate is still reported as "not sent by relay").
Size: 15 minutes either way.
evidence: $ wc -l signals.log -> 48;  uniq -c: 37 "sent SIGKILL to group N: gate: its command ended, ...", 6 "sent SIGTERM to pid N: no reason given", 5 "bin/ci: the time limit of the gate ran out"
tests/conftest.py:1-2: "so a test that forgets to set them cannot read or write the owner's ~/.claude, ~/.relay"
failing_case: relay gate runs bin/ci with RELAY_SIGNAL_LOG=~/.relay/signals.log (relay_gate.py:476); pytest inherits it and the
per-test switch does not touch it. Running tests/test_gate.py alone wrote 48 lines (37 "gate: its command ended" SIGKILL
cleanups, 6 leftover stops, 5 bin/ci time-limit stops) into the log the environment named. Under a real gate these go
to the owner's live ~/.relay/signals.log, which tests/conftest.py:1-2 says a test cannot write. Nothing ever trims it.
fix_hint: (a) keep the inheritance, add a cap in record_sent (trim to the last N lines when the file passes a size) and name the
exception in tests/conftest.py; or (b) temporary_environment sets RELAY_SIGNAL_LOG to a run-wide file in RUN_TEMP.
pass_cases: 1. The owner's choice is written down in tests/conftest.py's docstring (the exception, or none).
2. If the run-wide temp log is chosen: a gate's tests write no line to $RELAY_HOME/signals.log of the outer gate; a nested gate in a test still finds a stop another test of the same run sent.
3. If the live log is kept: the log has a bound (for example kept to the last N lines or N days) and a test shows an old line is dropped.
reason: Carried over from the earlier check; files unchanged since.
findings.summary: under a gate every test now appends to the owner's ~/.relay/signals.log, against the test harness's promise that no test writes the owner's ~/.relay; the file is never pruned

but the item's promise is every sender, and the shared log is the only place a later trace can look. bin/check is a

pass_cases: 1. bin/check with CHECK_TIMEOUT=1 on a step that sleeps: the signal log gains "sent SIGTERM to group <step pid>: bin/check: the step passed its time bound".

details: CONFIRMED by reading run(): returncode is unknown on the exception path but the same reason is written. A reader
tracing a SIGKILL of a command would be told the wrong cause. Size: 10 minutes.
evidence: lib/relay_gate.py:565-568 finally: record_sent(proc.pid, True, SIGKILL, "gate: its command ended, ...") on every exit path
failing_case: relay gate gets SIGTERM while bin/ci runs: the handler raises, the finally SIGKILLs the command's group and writes
"gate: its command ended, the command's group is cleaned up". The command had not ended; the gate was stopped.
Should read e.g. "gate: the gate was stopped (SIGTERM), its command's group is ended".
fix_hint: Choose the reason from whether proc.returncode is set (proc.poll() is not None) before the record.
pass_cases: 1. A gate stopped by SIGTERM while its command sleeps: the signal log line for the command's group names the gate's stop.
2. A gate whose command ended by itself: the line keeps "its command ended".
reason: Carried over; test passes on head.
findings.summary: the gate's group SIGKILL is logged as 'its command ended' also when the gate itself was stopped and is killing a running command

details: CONFIRMED by reading. Edge cases only. Size: 10 minutes.
evidence: lib/relay_procs.py: re.match(r"t=([0-9.]+) (relay pid .* sent \S+ to (?:pid|group) (\d+): .*)", line)
failing_case: record_sent swallows OSError (unwritable ~/.relay) and sent_by_relay returns None on OSError; signal_line then states
"not sent by relay". Also record_sent writes "sent signal 99 to ..." for an unnamed signal, which the reader's regex
(`sent \S+ to`) cannot match.
fix_hint: Return a distinct value for an unreadable log and word the line accordingly; use `sent .+? to` in the regex.
pass_cases: 1. sent_by_relay on a missing log: signal_line says the log could not be read, not "not sent by relay".
2. record_sent(pid, False, 99, "x") then sent_by_relay(pid, 0) finds the line.
3. A readable log with no matching line: still "not sent by relay".
reason: tests/test_gate_stops.py:331-342 passes on head with the new wording.
findings.summary: a log that cannot be read or written, or a signal with no name, is reported as 'not sent by relay'
